1.  The petition had been listed together on previous dates before the Court, with other similarly placed matters where quashing was sought by the respective petitioners of FIRs involving s. 304A IPC on the basis of settlement with the legal heirs of the deceased.

The petitions were tagged together for assessment of the point of law whether relief for quashing in these petitions could be allowed or not considering that offence punishable under s. 304A IPC was not compoundable.

In one of these petitions which were tagged together viz. Ajay Agarwal v. State of NCT of Delhi Crim.
M.C. No. 2899 of 2018, this Court after an assessment of the relevant decisions of the Hon'ble Supreme Court and this Court has opined that the courts are not prohibited per se in entertaining such petitions for quashing and granting the relief as prayed, and can indeed permit quashing of the FIR involving a section 304A IPC offence on settlement between the parties,

This could be done for various reasons inter alia, if a conspectus of the facts and evidence as adduced showed prima facie that there was no criminal negligence or no mens rea (in that it would be difficult to secure a conviction); or that considering the social/economic situation of the family of the deceased it would be preferable to provide adequate compensation than await the conclusion of trial/appeal (in other words put a quietus to the matter);
or that since the family of the deceased having accepted compensation which was adequate (being either endorsed or enhanced by the court) the continuance of the proceedings would be an exercise in futility; or otherwise taking into account other tangible and intangible circumstances as the court may assess in interaction with the parties and allow the prayers in the interest of justice.
These petitions have now been de-tagged considering that the facts and circumstances of each case would have to be appreciated separately and individually, by the Court.

This petition has been filed for quashing of FIR No.223/2017 PS Mian Wali Nagar under Sections 279/304A IPC and Sections 146/196 of the MV Act, on ground of settlement arrived at before the MACT Court, Tis Hazari on 06th December, 2017.
It was noted in the said order that the matter had been settled amicably for a settlement amount of Rs.5 lacs which was to be paid to the LRs of the deceased i.e. respondent Nos.3-9.

Respondent No.3 had appeared on the last occasion and stated that she is satisfied with the settlement and has received an amount of Rs.4 lacs already and is not interested in going ahead with the proceedings.
As regards the remaining amount of Rs.1 lac which is being tendered today vide DD This is a digitally signed order.

The Order is downloaded from the DHC Server on 24/09/2023 at 09:28:07 No.007954 dated 27.02.2023 drawn from Bank of Baroda to the respondent No.4, the son of the deceased who is present in Court and duly identified by the IO.
3. On an assessment of the facts and circumstances in this petition, this Court is of the opinion that it would be prudent to put a quietus to the matter, in the interests of justice.

Considering the above settlement between the parties and the chances of conviction of the petitioners being remote and bleak, there is no use in continuing with proceedings of the present FIR as it would be a misuse of the process of the Court and an unnecessary burden on the State exchequer.
Accordingly, the petition is allowed.
Consequently, the FIR No.223/2017 PS Mian Wali Nagar is quashed to the extent of offences under Sections 279/304A IPC.

However, as regards offences under Sections 146/196 of the MV Act, these relate to offences against the state and violation of special regulatory provisions under the Motor Vehicles Act and therefore the State will continue to prosecute the same.
4. Parties shall abide by the terms of settlement.
5. Accordingly, the petition is disposed of.
Pending applications (if any) are disposed of as infructuous.
6. Order be uploaded on the website of this Court.
ANISH DAYAL, J MAY 16, 2023/MK
